data.title: Mastercard (MA) Q3 Earnings Underline Margin Strength Behind A Quiet Stock Move
data.description:
Mastercard came into this Q3 2026 print riding strong momentum, with the stock up double digits over the past month and edging another 0.4% higher to about US$638 today. The move looks modest compared with what the numbers just delivered. Net revenue reached US$9.8b and basic earnings per share came in at US$5.29, both reinforcing a powerful profit trend.

The market reaction so far suggests a shrug. The financial story points to something sturdier, as Mastercard continues to convert payment volumes into high margin earnings power that long term holders have been betting on.

  • Net Income (Excl. Extra Items) (Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025): US$4,628m vs. US$3,927m (up 17.9%)
  • Basic EPS (Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025): US$5.29 vs. US$4.35 (up 21.7%)
  • Net Profit Margin, trailing 12 months (latest year vs prior year): 46.7% vs. 45.3% (higher margin level; earnings up 19% year on year)

Mastercard is betting big on agentic commerce with OpenAI. Ask Charlie what Mastercard’s OpenAI deal could mean for earnings.

Mastercard’s Asset-Light Rail Model Under the Microscope

"It never lends money and never holds credit risk on its books, it just takes a small cut every time a transaction crosses its network. That's the whole business model, and it's a remarkably good one: high margins, low capital intensity, and growth tied to the slow global shift away from cash."

Q3 results support this toll‑booth description. Mastercard converted a 14% rise in net revenue into 18% higher net income and 22% higher basic EPS, while the trailing 12‑month net profit margin edged up to 46.7%. That widening margin, even as operating expenses increased at a double‑digit clip, points to the fee‑based, low capital burden model still working as advertised.

Testing Fears Of Disruption To Mastercard’s Moat

"Mastercard isn't standing still while stablecoins reshape payments. It is building settlement infrastructure and tools for 'agentic commerce' around them instead of fighting the trend. Whether that becomes a meaningful new revenue stream or just defends the existing one, it argues for the moat holding rather than eroding, and gives the company a second growth story to lean on if card volumes ever slow."

The concern is that new rails and AI agents erode Mastercard’s role. Q3 data does not yet show that pressure winning out. Cross‑border volume rose 11%, value‑added services grew 19%, and management highlighted early traction in agentic commerce and stablecoin infrastructure through the Global Money Platform and Arc. Regulatory and A2A competition remain live risks, but transaction and services trends this quarter lean toward moat defence rather than slippage.

data.title: Earnings Beat: Nitto Denko Corporation Just Beat Analyst Forecasts, And Analysts Have Been Updating Their Models
data.description:
Last week, you might have seen that Nitto Denko Corporation (TSE:6988) released its half-year result to the market. The early response was not positive, with shares down 4.9% to JP¥3,392 in the past week. Revenues were JP¥558b, approximately in line with expectations, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) performed substantially better. EPS of JP¥64.57 were also better than expected, beating analyst predictions by 15%. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following the latest results, Nitto Denko's ten analysts are now forecasting revenues of JP¥1.11t in 2027. This would be an okay 3.3% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to rise 2.8% to JP¥218. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of JP¥1.11t and earnings per share (EPS) of JP¥219 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Nitto Denko

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of JP¥3,800, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. The consensus price target is just an average of individual analyst targets, so - it could be handy to see how wide the range of underlying estimates is. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Nitto Denko at JP¥4,500 per share, while the most bearish prices it at JP¥3,200. These price targets show that analysts do have some differing views on the business, but the estimates do not vary enough to suggest to us that some are betting on wild success or utter failure.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. It's clear from the latest estimates that Nitto Denko's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with the forecast 6.7% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 noticeably faster than its historical growth of 4.7% p.a. over the past five years. Compare this with other companies in the same industry, which are forecast to grow their revenue 5.6% annually. Nitto Denko is expected to grow at about the same rate as its industry, so it's not clear that we can draw any conclusions from its growth relative to competitors.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. They also reconfirmed their revenue estimates, with the company predicted to grow at about the same rate as the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at JP¥3,800, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.
